name: Borage
grown_as: A hardy annual herb that seeds itself about.
habit: A coarse, bushy, branched annual 40 to 90 cm, the thick hollow stems covered in stiff white bristles, with drooping clusters of blue stars at the top.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at first, then alternate up the stem
leaf.outline: Oval to oblong-lance-shaped, 5 to 20 cm long
leaf.base: Lower leaves narrow into a winged stalk; upper leaves stalkless, half-clasping the stem
leaf.veins: A network pressed in from above, making the leaf wrinkled
leaf.surface: Rough, covered in stiff white bristly hairs, dull
leaf.stalk: Lower leaves on a broad winged stalk; upper leaves none
leaf.colour: Dull mid to dark green, greyish from the hairs

flower.form: A flat five-pointed star, hanging face down
flower.petals: Five, joined only at the very base, spreading flat, each a pointed triangle
flower.colour: Bright clear blue; pink in bud and sometimes pinkish as they fade; rarely white
flower.centre: A cone of near-black anthers pointing forward from the middle, with a small ring of white scales at its base
flower.behind: Five narrow, pointed, bristly green sepals showing between the petals
flower.carried: In loose, branched, drooping clusters at the tops of the stems, the flowers nodding down on hairy stalks

fruit: Four nutlets inside the persistent bristly calyx, which closes up and hangs down. Seeds oblong, ridged and wrinkled, dark brown to black, about 5 mm, with a pale collar at one end.
seedling: Two large, broad oval seed leaves on short stalks, slightly hairy, then oval bristly first leaves
winter: None: an annual, killed by hard frost.

leaf: wrinkled surface, winged stalk on lower leaves
bloom: a flat five-pointed star of bright blue petals
a black cone of anthers in the middle
narrow bristly green sepals showing between the petals
seed: oblong ridged dark brown-black seeds with a pale collar
seedling: two large broad oval seed leaves
first true leaves oval and bristly
young: a rosette of large rough bristly oval leaves
flower: drooping clusters of blue star flowers facing down
pink buds among the blue flowers
seedhead: drooping clusters of closed bristly calyces holding dark seeds

look_alikes: Comfrey has hanging tubular bells, not stars. Green alkanet (Pentaglottis sempervirens) is perennial with smaller, deep blue flowers with a white eye and no black cone. Viper's-bugloss has narrow leaves and funnel-shaped flowers in spikes.
